description: Tech Spatranzz is an enthusiastic, innovation-driven team based in Chennai, specializing in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and advanced software development. United by a passion for space exploration and cutting-edge tech, we are tackling the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge to build intelligent, reliable navigation frameworks. We are seeking passionate developers, data analysts, and space enthusiasts to join our team. Let’s build the future together!
summary:
The Lunar Learning Portal is an interactive web-based educational platform designed to help students, educators, and space enthusiasts explore the Moon in an engaging and accessible way. The project addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge by leveraging [NASA lunar datasets — name them, e.g., LRO LOLA DEM data, LADEE, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter] to build visualizations and learning modules about lunar geography, mission history, and scientific concepts. Users can navigate interactive lunar maps, explore key landing sites, and access curated educational content.

This project is important because lunar literacy is essential for inspiring the next generation of scientists and engineers, and for building public support for NASA's Artemis program. By making complex lunar science accessible through interactive tools, the portal bridges the gap between raw NASA data and classroom learning. The platform was built using [tech stack — e.g., React, Python, D3.js] and powered by [specific NASA data sources] to deliver a seamless, informative experience.
details:
What does it do / How does it work?

The Lunar Learning Portal is a [web application / static site / interactive dashboard] that provides an immersive way to explore lunar science and geography. Key features include:

  • Interactive lunar map — Users can explore the Moon's surface, zoom into specific regions, and view terrain data [mention tools: e.g., D3.js, WebGL, Cesium, Mapbox].
  • Educational content modules — Curated lessons about [lunar geography, NASA missions, lunar geology, the Artemis program, etc.].
  • Data visualization — Charts, 3D models, or overlays based on [NASA datasets] that illustrate [elevation, mineral composition, landing site locations, etc.].
  • [Any other features — quizzes, mission timelines, AR viewer, etc.]

What benefits does it have?

  • Makes NASA's lunar data accessible to non-experts and classroom settings
  • Supports STEM education with hands-on exploration tools
  • Serves as a supplement for educators teaching space science, geography, or physics
  • Encourages public engagement with NASA's Artemis initiatives

What is the intended impact?

The portal aims to inspire interest in space exploration among students and the general public, provide educators with ready-to-use lunar science resources, and demonstrate how open NASA data can be transformed into meaningful educational experiences.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: [e.g., React / HTML, CSS, JavaScript / Vue.js / Next.js]
  • Backend (if any): [e.g., Python Flask / Node.js / None — static site]
  • Data visualization: [e.g., D3.js / Three.js / Cesium / Plotly]
  • Data sources: [e.g., NASA APIs, LRO data, PDS Geoscience Node]
  • Hosting: [e.g., GitHub Pages / Vercel / Netlify]
  • Other tools: [e.g., Figma for design, VS Code, Git]

What is your project creative? What factors did your team consider?

  • We combined raw NASA scientific data with user-friendly visual storytelling — making technical datasets approachable for general audiences.
  • We prioritized accessibility and performance, ensuring the site works on mobile and desktop.
  • We considered educational pedagogy — structuring content to support both self-guided exploration and structured classroom use.
  • Creativity was shown through [interactive elements, unique data overlays, storytelling approach, etc.].
